title: The Build track is the manual path and Vetra Studio is the AI-guided one, and both produce the same kind of package so a project can switch between them
content:
The Academy states the fork explicitly at the top of the Build chapter: this is the **manual experience** — building packages by hand with the Powerhouse CLI, controlling document models, editors, processors and publishing — while the **AI-guided experience** lives in Vetra Studio, where you describe what you want in chat and the agent writes the specs and code, with **no local setup required**.

The important part is the sentence that follows: "the two paths produce the same kind of package, so you can mix and match — prototype with the agent, then drop down to the manual workflow for fine-grained control." That makes the choice reversible rather than architectural.

For the manual path the machine needs three things — **Node.js 24** to run the code, **VS Code** to write it, **Git** to manage it — plus the CLI: `pnpm install -g ph-cmd` (or npm), with a global install recommended so the command works from any directory. If those three are already present, installing `ph-cmd` is the only step.

**Windows users are steered to WSL** rather than native Windows: `wsl --install` in an Administrator PowerShell, restart, create a Linux user, then follow the Linux (Ubuntu/Debian) instructions throughout. The stated reason is a development experience consistent with production environments and with most tutorials; VS Code still runs on Windows through the Remote-WSL extension.
